tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

5	import json

11	import urllib.request
12	from typing import Any, Mapping
13	
14	
15	SERVER_NAME = "spaces-rowboat"
16	SERVER_VERSION = "1.0.0"
17	PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2024-11-05"
18	REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5
19	
20	TOOLS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{
21	    "name": "rowboat_status",
22	    "description": "Read the configured Rowboat HTTP status using HEAD.",
23	    "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": False},
24	}]
25	
26	
27	class ToolError(Exception):
28	    """Expected, safe-to-return tool error."""
29	
30	    def __init__(self, message: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
31	        super().__init__(message)
32	        self.payload = dict(payload or {"error": message})
33	
34	
35	class _NoRedirectHandler(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
36	    """Preserve the original HEAD request and expose every 3xx response."""
37	
38	    def redirect_request(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
39	        return None
40	
41	
42	def _open_head_without_redirect(request: urllib.request.Request, *, timeout: float):
43	    """Open one HEAD request without following or converting redirects."""
44	    return urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirectHandler()).open(request, timeout=timeout)
45	
46	
47	def _invalid_url() -> ToolError:
48	    return ToolError("configuration_error: ROWBOAT_URL is invalid")
49	
50	
51	def _is_noncanonical_numeric_host(hostname: str) -> bool:
52	    labels = hostname.split(".")
53	    return (
54	        hostname.isdigit()
55	        or hostname.startswith(("0x", "0o"))
56	        or (len(labels) > 1 and all(label.isdigit() for label in labels))
57	    )
58	
59	
60	def _rowboat_url(env: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
61	    raw_url = (env.get("ROWBOAT_URL") or "").strip()
62	    if not raw_url:
63	        raise ToolError("configuration_error: ROWBOAT_URL is required")
64	    try:
65	        parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw_url)
66	        hostname = (parsed.hostname or "").rstrip(".").lower()
67	        _ = parsed.port
68	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
69	        raise _invalid_url() from None
70	    if (
71	        parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"}
72	        or not parsed.netloc
73	        or parsed.query
74	        or parsed.fragment
75	    ):
76	        raise _invalid_url()
77	    if parsed.username is not None or parsed.password is not None:
78	        raise _invalid_url()
79	    if hostname == "localhost" or hostname.endswith(".localhost"):
80	        raise _invalid_url()
81	    try:
82	        address = ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)
83	    except ValueError:
84	        if _is_noncanonical_numeric_host(hostname):
85	            raise _invalid_url()
86	    else:
87	        mapped = getattr(address, "ipv4_mapped", None)
88	        if (
89	            address.is_loopback
90	            or address.is_unspecified
91	            or (mapped is not None and (mapped.is_loopback or mapped.is_unspecified))
92	        ):
93	            raise _invalid_url()
94	    return raw_url.rstrip("/")
95	
96	
97	def rowboat_status(env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
98	    """Probe the explicitly configured service once; never use a fallback URL."""
99	    url = _rowboat_url(env or os.environ)
100	    try:
101	        request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="HEAD")
102	        with _open_head_without_redirect(request, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:
103	            status = int(response.getcode())
104	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
105	        return {
106	            "ok": 200 <= exc.code < 400,
107	            "source": "rowboat-http",
108	            "url": url,
109	            "http_status": exc.code,
110	        }
111	    except Exception as exc:
112	        raise ToolError(
113	            "rowboat_unverified",
114	            {"ok": False, "source": "rowboat-http", "url": url, "error": type(exc).__name__},
115	        ) from exc
116	    return {
117	        "ok": 200 <= status < 400,
118	        "source": "rowboat-http",
119	        "url": url,
120	        "http_status": status,
121	    }
122	
123	
124	def _tool_result(payload: Mapping[str, Any], *, is_error: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
125	    return {
126	        "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)}],
127	        "isError": is_error,
128	    }
129	
130	
131	def handle_message(message: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
132	    request_id = message.get("id")
133	    method = message.get("method")
134	    if method == "notifications/initialized":
135	        return None
136	    if method == "initialize":
137	        return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": {
138	            "protocolVersion": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
139	            "serverInfo": {"name": SERVER_NAME, "version": SERVER_VERSION},
140	            "capabilities": {"tools": {}},
141	        }}
142	    if method == "tools/list":
143	        return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": {"tools": TOOLS}}
144	    if method == "tools/call":
145	        params = message.get("params")
146	        if not isinstance(params, Mapping) or params.get("name") != "rowboat_status":
147	            return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": _tool_result(
148	                {"error": "unknown_tool: rowboat_status is the only supported tool"}, is_error=True,
149	            )}
150	        arguments = params.get("arguments", {})
151	        if not isinstance(arguments, Mapping):
152	            return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": _tool_result(
153	                {"error": "invalid_arguments: arguments must be an object"}, is_error=True,
154	            )}
155	        if arguments:
156	            return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": _tool_result(
157	                {"error": "invalid_arguments: rowboat_status accepts no arguments"}, is_error=True,
158	            )}
159	        try:
160	            payload = rowboat_status()
161	            return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": _tool_result(payload)}
162	        except ToolError as exc:
163	            return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "result": _tool_result(exc.payload, is_error=True)}
164	    return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "error": {"code": -32601, "message": "method not found"}}
165	
166	
167	def main() -> int:
168	    for line in sys.stdin:
169	        if not line.strip():
170	            continue
171	        try:
172	            message = json.loads(line)
173	            if not isinstance(message, Mapping):
174	                raise ValueError("request must be an object")
175	            response = handle_message(message)
176	        except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
177	            response = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": None, "error": {"code": -32700, "message": "parse error"}}
178	        if response is not None:
179	            print(json.dumps(response, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
180	    return 0
181	
182	
183	if __name__ == "__main__":
184	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	# CLAUDE.md - AI Coding Agent Context
2	
3	This file provides context for AI coding agents working on the Rowboat monorepo.
4	
5	## Quick Reference Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	# Electron App (apps/x)
9	cd apps/x && pnpm install          # Install dependencies
10	cd apps/x && npm run deps          # Build workspace packages (shared → core → preload)
11	cd apps/x && npm run dev           # Development mode (builds deps, runs app)
12	cd apps/x && npm run lint          # Lint check
13	cd apps/x/apps/main && npm run package   # Production build (.app)
14	cd apps/x/apps/main && npm run make      # Create DMG distributable
15	```
16	
17	## Monorepo Structure
18	
19	```
20	rowboat/
21	├── apps/
22	│   ├── x/                 # Electron desktop app (focus of this doc)
23	│   ├── rowboat/           # Next.js web dashboard
24	│   ├── rowboatx/          # Next.js frontend
25	│   ├── cli/               # CLI tool
26	│   ├── python-sdk/        # Python SDK
27	│   └── docs/              # Documentation site
28	├── CLAUDE.md              # This file
29	└── README.md              # User-facing readme
30	```
31	
32	## Electron App Architecture (`apps/x`)
33	
34	The Electron app is a **nested pnpm workspace** with its own package management.
35	
36	```
37	apps/x/
38	├── package.json           # Workspace root, dev scripts
39	├── pnpm-workspace.yaml    # Defines workspace packages
40	├── pnpm-lock.yaml         # Lockfile
41	├── apps/
42	│   ├── main/              # Electron main process
43	│   │   ├── src/           # Main process source
44	│   │   ├── forge.config.cjs   # Electron Forge config
45	│   │   └── bundle.mjs     # esbuild bundler
46	│   ├── renderer/          # React UI (Vite)
47	│   │   ├── src/           # React components
48	│   │   └── vite.config.ts
49	│   └── preload/           # Electron preload scripts
50	│       └── src/
51	└── packages/
52	    ├── shared/            # @x/shared - Types, utilities, validators
53	    └── core/              # @x/core - Business logic, AI, OAuth, MCP
54	```
55	
56	### Build Order (Dependencies)
57	
58	```
59	shared (no deps)
60	   ↓
61	core (depends on shared)
62	   ↓
63	preload (depends on shared)
64	   ↓
65	renderer (depends on shared)
66	main (depends on shared, core)
67	```
68	
69	**The `npm run deps` command builds:** shared → core → preload
70	
71	### Key Entry Points
72	
73	| Component | Entry | Output |
74	|-----------|-------|--------|
75	| main | `apps/main/src/main.ts` | `.package/dist/main.cjs` |
76	| renderer | `apps/renderer/src/main.tsx` | `apps/renderer/dist/` |
77	| preload | `apps/preload/src/preload.ts` | `apps/preload/dist/preload.js` |
78	
79	## Build System
80	
81	- **Package manager:** pnpm (required for `workspace:*` protocol)
82	- **Main bundler:** esbuild (bundles to single CommonJS file)
83	- **Renderer bundler:** Vite
84	- **Packaging:** Electron Forge
85	- **TypeScript:** ES2022 target
86	
87	### Why esbuild bundling?
88	
89	pnpm uses symlinks for workspace packages. Electron Forge's dependency walker can't follow these symlinks. esbuild bundles everything into a single file, eliminating the need for node_modules in the packaged app.
90	
91	## Key Files Reference
92	
93	| Purpose | File |
94	|---------|------|
95	| Electron main entry | `apps/x/apps/main/src/main.ts` |
96	| React app entry | `apps/x/apps/renderer/src/main.tsx` |
97	| Forge config (packaging) | `apps/x/apps/main/forge.config.cjs` |
98	| Main process bundler | `apps/x/apps/main/bundle.mjs` |
99	| Vite config | `apps/x/apps/renderer/vite.config.ts` |
100	| Shared types | `apps/x/packages/shared/src/` |
101	| Core business logic | `apps/x/packages/core/src/` |
102	| Workspace config | `apps/x/pnpm-workspace.yaml` |
103	| Root scripts | `apps/x/package.json` |
104	
105	## Common Tasks
106	
107	### LLM configuration (single provider)
108	- Config file: `~/.rowboat/config/models.json`
109	- Schema: `{ provider: { flavor, apiKey?, baseURL?, headers? }, model: string }`
110	- Models catalog cache: `~/.rowboat/config/models.dev.json` (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google only)
111	
112	### Add a new shared type
113	1. Edit `apps/x/packages/shared/src/`
114	2. Run `cd apps/x && npm run deps` to rebuild
115	
116	### Modify main process
117	1. Edit `apps/x/apps/main/src/`
118	2. Restart dev server (main doesn't hot-reload)
119	
120	### Modify renderer (React UI)
121	1. Edit `apps/x/apps/renderer/src/`
122	2. Changes hot-reload automatically in dev mode
123	
124	### Add a new dependency to main
125	1. `cd apps/x/apps/main && pnpm add <package>`
126	2. Import in source - esbuild will bundle it
127	
128	### Verify compilation
129	```bash
130	cd apps/x && npm run deps && npm run lint
131	```
132	
133	## Tech Stack
134	
135	| Layer | Technology |
136	|-------|------------|
137	| Desktop | Electron 39.x |
138	| UI | React 19, Vite 7 |
139	| Styling | TailwindCSS, Radix UI |
140	| State | React hooks |

142	| IPC | Electron contextBridge |

  # A single-node REPLICA SET, not a standalone. Every plugin write -- the
  # catalog load, an installation with its admission rows and provider
  # bindings, the migration apply -- runs in one transaction, and a standalone
  # mongod refuses transactions outright (`repository_transaction_failed`).
  # One node is enough for that; it is still a replica set.
  mongo:
    image: mongo:latest
    command: ["mongod", "--replSet", "rs0", "--bind_ip_all"]
    ports:
      - "27017:27017"
    restart: unless-stopped
    attach: false
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    healthcheck:
      # Healthy only once the set is initiated AND this node is primary, so
      # dependents do not start against a node that cannot yet accept writes.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "mongosh --quiet --eval 'db.hello().isWritablePrimary' | grep -q true"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 10s

  # Initiates the set once and exits. Idempotent: an already-initiated set
  # answers `AlreadyInitialized`, which is success for our purposes.
  mongo-init:
    image: mongo:latest
    depends_on:
      - mongo
    restart: "no"
    attach: false
    entrypoint:
      - bash
      - -c
      - |
        for i in $$(seq 1 60); do
          mongosh --host mongo:27017 --quiet --eval 'quit(0)' && break
          sleep 2
        done
        mongosh --host mongo:27017 --quiet --eval '
          try { rs.status(); print("already initiated"); }
          catch (e) { rs.initiate({_id: "rs0", members: [{_id: 0, host: "mongo:27017"}]}); }
        '

## Rowboat space: exploration report
Base path: `C:/Users/User/Desktop/ehl-munich-2026/vibemind-os/spaces/rowboat`

### 1. What it is
- **The space ("Roarboot")** is a Python wrapper for the VibeMind host. It talks to a dockerised Rowboat app over HTTP or the Python SDK. Its features are knowledge-graph search, email drafting, meeting briefs, decks and Docker control (docstring in `__init__.py`).
- **`rowboat/` is a vendored fork of upstream rowboatlabs/rowboat.** It sits inside the `Flissel/vibemind-os` repo, not as a submodule (`rowboat/README.md`, `rowboat/CLAUDE.md`). It has been heavily customised: German-named MCP tools, an OpenAI plugin runtime, and a Mongo replica set.
- **Main app:** `rowboat/apps/rowboat` is Next.js (App Router, turbopack) with TypeScript, zod, Tailwind and Auth0 (optional). It is laid out in clean-architecture style under `src/{entities,application,infrastructure,interface-adapters}`.
- **Infrastructure:** MongoDB is the database. Redis and Qdrant (vector RAG) are optional. Composio and Klavis provide integrations.
- **`rowboat/apps/x` (Electron desktop app) is a stub:** only `apps/x/apps/renderer` exists, and `packages/` is missing.
- **Python entry points:**
  - `mcp_server.py`: stdio MCP server, read-only status probe.
  - `knowledge_mcp_server.py`: stdio MCP server for the Brain T2 Markdown vault (`~/.rowboat/knowledge` or `KNOWLEDGE_DIR`). It writes through `core.knowledge.tresor` from `../../brain/the_brain`.
- **Broken import:** `__init__.py` imports `.config`, `.agents` and `.broadcast`, but none of these files exist. Importing the package fails; `tests/test_openai_plugin_runtime_contract.py` (lines 29-35) documents this and works around it.

### 2. Data model
Entity models are zod schemas in `rowboat/apps/rowboat/src/entities/models/`:
- `project.ts`, `project-member.ts`, `user.ts`, `api-key.ts`
- `conversation.ts`, `turn.ts`
- `job.ts`
- `scheduled-job-rule.ts`, `recurring-job-rule.ts`
- `composio-trigger-deployment.ts`, `composio-trigger-type.ts`
- `data-source.ts`, `data-source-doc.ts` (knowledge/RAG)
- `copilot.ts`, `assistant-template.ts`

Workflow types are in `rowboat/apps/rowboat/app/lib/types/workflow_types.ts`. A workflow is made of agents (conversation/pipeline/etc.), prompts, tools and pipelines, plus a `startAgent`.

**There are no Task or Kanban entities.** "Projects" are agent-workflow projects, not PM projects.

### 3. Scheduling and timed sending (exists and is usable)
- **One-shot schedules:** a `ScheduledJobRule` has `nextRunAt`, a status of pending/processing/triggered, and input messages.
- **Recurring schedules:** a `RecurringJobRule` has a `cron` expression (minute resolution), `nextRunAt` and `disabled`.
- **Jobs:** a `Job` records why it ran (`composio_trigger`, `scheduled_job_rule` or `recurring_job_rule`) and has a status of pending/running/completed/failed.
- **Workers:**
  - `src/application/workers/job-rules.worker.ts` polls both rule types each minute and turns due rules into jobs.
  - `src/application/workers/jobs.worker.ts` runs the jobs.
  - Scripts: `app/scripts/jobs-worker.ts` (`npm run jobs-worker`, which is the `jobs-worker` compose service) and `app/scripts/job-rules.worker.ts`.
- **Use cases:** `src/application/use-cases/{scheduled-job-rules,recurring-job-rules,jobs,composio-trigger-deployments}`.
- **How a send works:** a job feeds messages into the project's agent workflow. The actual email or post goes out through agent tools (Composio/Klavis, e.g. Gmail).
- **Outside Rowboat:** `spaces/marketing/n8n_workflows/` holds broadcast flows (`04_linkedin`, `05_x`, `07_discord`, `08_telegram`, `03_approval_orchestrator`).

### 4. UI and API
- **UI:** Next.js pages under `app/projects/[projectId]/`: `workflow/`, `jobs/`, `manage-triggers/{scheduled,recurring,triggers}`, `conversations/`, `sources/`, `tools/`, `playground/`, `plugins/`, `config/`. The jobs and trigger pages are a ready-made scheduling UI to build on.
- **API:** `app/api/`:
  - `v1/[projectId]/chat`
  - `v1/projects/[projectId]/...`
  - `v1/plugins`, `v1/plugin-session`
  - `mcp/` (route.ts and rpc.ts, Bearer API key)
  - `composio`, `twilio`, `widget`, `uploads`, `stream-response`
  - Server actions live in `app/actions/`.

### 5. MCP tools
- **`mcp_server.py`:** `rowboat_status` sends a HEAD probe to `ROWBOAT_URL` and rejects localhost.
- **`knowledge_mcp_server.py`:**
  - `knowledge_list`: list vault documents.
  - `knowledge_read`: read one Markdown document.
  - `knowledge_write`: write a document, only after its sources are verified (Tresor check).
- **Next.js MCP (`app/api/mcp/rpc.ts`):**
  - `rowboat_wissensquellen`: list data sources.
  - `rowboat_wissensquelle`: get one source.
  - `rowboat_dokumente`: list docs.
  - `rowboat_datei_url`: get a file URL.
  - `rowboat_quelle_anlegen`: create a source.
  - `rowboat_dokumente_schreiben`: write docs.
- **Python host tools (not MCP):** in `tools/roarboot_tools.py`, `tools/docker_tools.py` and `tools/roarboot_client.py`: chat, search_knowledge, query_knowledge, draft_email, generate_meeting_brief, generate_deck, process_voice_note, rag_search, upload_document, explore_graph, open_webview, start_docker, stop_docker, restart_docker, docker_status.

### 6. Integration points
- **Host contract:** the space exports agents, tools and workers through `__init__.py`.
  - `workers/roarboot_workers.py` depends on `swarm.workers.base_worker`, `spaces.SpaceType.ROWBOAT` and `swarm.event_bus`, none of which are in this repo.
  - The docstring says the space listens on Redis stream `events:tasks:roarboot` and broadcasts to the Electron WebView.
  - `workers/update_checker.py` auto-pulls upstream releases.
- **Marketing space:**
  - `spaces/marketing/tools/rowboat_client.py` POSTs to `/api/v1/{project}/chat`, with n8n calling back to `/api/curator/rowboat_callback/{id}`.
  - `spaces/marketing/workers/bubble_rowboat_export.py` uses the Rowboat MCP tools.
- **No sales space exists** (only `marketing/` and `rowboat/`).

### 7. Running locally
- **Main stack:** `rowboat/start.sh` runs `docker compose` with profiles qdrant, setup_qdrant and rag-worker, then `up --build`. Services are rowboat (:3000), rowboat_agents (host port 3101), jobs-worker, mongo (replica set rs0, initialised by mongo-init), redis and qdrant.
- **Missing build contexts:** compose references `./apps/rowboat_agents` and `./apps/docs`, but neither directory exists. As written, the build will fail for those services.
- **Dev mode:** `cd rowboat/apps/rowboat && npm run dev`, plus `npm run jobs-worker`. This needs MongoDB (replica set) and Redis.
- **Env names, Next app and workers:** OPENAI_API_KEY, MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING, REDIS_URL, AGENTS_API_URL, AGENTS_API_KEY, USE_AUTH, AUTH0_*, PROVIDER_API_KEY, PROVIDER_BASE_URL, PROVIDER_DEFAULT_MODEL, PROVIDER_COPILOT_MODEL, USE_RAG*, QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY, USE_COMPOSIO_TOOLS, COMPOSIO_API_KEY, COMPOSIO_TRIGGERS_WEBHOOK_SECRET, USE_KLAVIS_TOOLS, KLAVIS_API_KEY, KLAVIS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, KLAVIS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, AWS_* / RAG_UPLOADS_S3_*, PLUGIN_UI_PREVIEW_SECRET, PLUGIN_MIGRATION_*, USE_BILLING / BILLING_*, CHAT_WIDGET_SESSION_JWT_SECRET.
- **Env names, Python side:** ROWBOAT_URL, ROWBOAT_API_KEY, ROWBOAT_PROJECT_ID, KNOWLEDGE_DIR, ROWBOAT_AUTO_START, ROWBOAT_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL, ROWBOAT_AUTO_PULL.

### Takeaway for the EHL PM extension
Scheduling already exists end to end: scheduled and cron rules, jobs, workers, UI pages, and Composio-based sending. What is missing is the PM layer: Task, Milestone and Event entities and an overview board. Those could sit next to `src/entities/models/` and `app/projects/[projectId]/`. Scheduled sends could then be modelled as ScheduledJobRules linked to tasks.
